message.content:
In this Go codebase (memos repo), find:

1. Memo creation/insert SQL: grep -rn "INSERT.*memo\|CreateMemo\|createMemo\|InsertMemo" --include="*.go" . | head -30
2. Default database driver: grep -rn "default.*driver\|defaultDriver\|sqlite\|SQLite" --include="*.go" . | head -30
3. Markdown parser interface and implementations: grep -rn "Parser\|Converter\|markdown\|Markdown" --include="*.go" . | head -40
4. find . -path "*markdown*" -name "*.go" | head -20
5. Memo visibility enforcement: grep -rn "Visibility\|visibility\|PRIVATE\|PUBLIC\|PROTECTED\|isVisible\|checkVisibility\|accessControl" --include="*.go" . | head -40
6. Memo metadata / property extraction: grep -rn "Property\|Snippet\|Preview\|snippet\|preview\|ExtractMetadata\|extractMetadata\|BuildPayload\|payload" --include="*.go" . | head -30
7. Memo content analysis / derived fields: grep -rn "func.*memo.*content\|analyzeContent\|parseContent\|ExtractContent" --include="*.go" . | head -20

Report findings with file paths and line numbers.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

39	// AllowAnonymous reports whether unauthenticated visitors may access the instance.
40	//
41	// Anonymous access is enabled only when an InstanceURL is configured. An instance
42	// with no InstanceURL set is treated as private: anonymous callers are limited to
43	// the auth-bootstrap endpoints (sign-in, share links, etc.) and the web UI redirects
44	// them to the sign-in page instead of the public Explore view. Authenticated callers
45	// (session, access token, or personal access token) are never affected.
46	func (p *Profile) AllowAnonymous() bool {
47		return strings.TrimSpace(p.InstanceURL) != ""
48	}

50	func checkDataDir(dataDir string) (string, error) {
51		// Convert to absolute path if relative path is supplied.
52		if !filepath.IsAbs(dataDir) {
53			// Use current working directory, not the binary's directory
54			// This ensures we use the actual working directory where the process runs
55			absDir, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir)
56			if err != nil {
57				return "", err
58			}
59			dataDir = absDir
60		}
61	
62		// Trim trailing \ or / in case user supplies
63		dataDir = strings.TrimRight(dataDir, "\\/")
64		if _, err := os.Stat(dataDir); err != nil {
65			return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "unable to access data folder %s", dataDir)
66		}
67		return dataDir, nil
68	}
69	
70	func (p *Profile) Validate() error {
71		// Set default data directory if not specified
72		if p.Data == "" {
73			if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
74				p.Data = filepath.Join(os.Getenv("ProgramData"), "memos")
75			} else {
76				// On Linux/macOS, check if /var/opt/memos exists and is writable (Docker scenario)
77				if info, err := os.Stat("/var/opt/memos"); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
78					// Check if we can write to this directory
79					testFile := filepath.Join("/var/opt/memos", ".write-test")
80					if err := os.WriteFile(testFile, []byte("test"), 0600); err == nil {
81						os.Remove(testFile)
82						p.Data = "/var/opt/memos"
83					} else {
84						// /var/opt/memos exists but is not writable, use current directory
85						slog.Warn("/var/opt/memos is not writable, using current directory")
86						p.Data = "."
87					}
88				} else {
89					// /var/opt/memos doesn't exist, use current directory (local development)
90					p.Data = "."
91				}
92			}
93		}
94	
95		// Create data directory if it doesn't exist
96		if _, err := os.Stat(p.Data); os.IsNotExist(err) {
97			if err := os.MkdirAll(p.Data, 0770); err != nil {
98				slog.Error("failed to create data directory", slog.String("data", p.Data), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
99				return err
100			}
101		}
102	
103		dataDir, err := checkDataDir(p.Data)
104		if err != nil {
105			slog.Error("failed to check dsn", slog.String("data", dataDir), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
106			return err
107		}
108	
109		p.Data = dataDir
110		if p.Driver == "sqlite" && p.DSN == "" {
111			mode := "prod"
112			if p.Demo {
113				mode = "demo"
114			}
115			dbFile := fmt.Sprintf("memos_%s.db", mode)
116			p.DSN = filepath.Join(dataDir, dbFile)
117		}
118	
119		return nil
120	}

Here is a comprehensive report of findings across all seven areas:

---

## 1. Memo Creation / Insert SQL

**Service layer** (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 70):
- `APIV1Service.CreateMemo()` is the main entry point. It validates the user, generates a UID, builds a `store.Memo` struct (with content, visibility, optional timestamps), calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload()` to extract markdown metadata, then delegates to `s.Store.CreateMemo()`.
- After creation it sets attachments/relations, dispatches webhooks, broadcasts SSE events, and handles @mention notifications.

**Store abstraction** (`/bench/repo/store/memo.go`, line 109):
- `Store.CreateMemo()` validates the UID against `base.UIDMatcher`, then calls `s.driver.CreateMemo()`.

**Driver interface** (`/bench/repo/store/driver.go`, line 29):
- `CreateMemo(ctx context.Context, create *Memo) (*Memo, error)` is defined in the `Driver` interface.

**SQLite implementation** (`/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go`, line 16-52):
- SQL: `INSERT INTO memo (uid, creator_id, content, visibility, payload [, created_ts] [, updated_ts]) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ? ...) RETURNING id, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status`

**PostgreSQL implementation** (`/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go`, line 16-49):
- Same shape: `INSERT INTO memo (...) VALUES ($1, $2, ...) RETURNING id, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status`

**MySQL implementation** (`/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo.go`, line 16):
- `INSERT INTO memo (...) VALUES (?, ?, ...)` (MySQL does not use RETURNING; it uses `LastInsertId`).

---

## 2. Default Database Driver

**Profile definition** (`/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go`, lines 29-30):
- `Driver string` with comment `// sqlite, mysql`

**Default DSN logic** (`/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go`, line 110):
- `if p.Driver == "sqlite" && p.DSN == "" { ... }` -- when the driver is "sqlite" and no DSN is explicitly set, it defaults to `memos_prod.db` (or `memos_demo.db` in demo mode) inside the data directory.
- There is no hardcoded "default" driver in the profile itself -- it must be set externally (e.g. via CLI flags or environment). However, the sqlite path is the only driver with automatic DSN generation, making it the implicit/typical default.

**Driver factory** (`/bench/repo/store/db/db.go`, lines 14-32):
- `NewDBDriver()` switches on `profile.Driver`: `"sqlite"`, `"mysql"`, `"postgres"`. Unknown values return an error.

---

## 3. Markdown Parser Interface and Implementations

**Interface** (`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, lines 31-55):
The `Service` interface defines:
- `ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)` -- single-pass extraction of tags, mentions, and properties
- `ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)`
- `ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)`
- `RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)` -- AST back to markdown
- `RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)` -- markdown to HTML
- `GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)` -- plain text summary
- `ValidateContent(content []byte) error`
- `RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)`

**Implementation** (`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, lines 57-113):
- Private struct `service` implements `Service`, backed by `goldmark.Markdown`.
- Constructor `NewService(opts ...Option)` accepts options `WithTagExtension()` and `WithMentionExtension()`.
- Uses `goldmark` with `extension.GFM` (GitHub Flavored Markdown) and custom extensions for tags and mentions.

**Supporting files** (found via `find`):
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/ast/tag.go` -- `TagNode` AST node
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/ast/mention.go` -- `MentionNode` AST node
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/parser/tag.go` -- tag parser
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/parser/mention.go` -- mention parser
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/extensions/tag.go` -- goldmark tag extension
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/extensions/mention.go` -- goldmark mention extension
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go` -- renders AST back to markdown text

---

## 4. Markdown-related Go files

All located under `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/`:
- `markdown.go`, `markdown_test.go`
- `renderer/markdown_renderer.go`, `renderer/markdown_renderer_test.go`
- `parser/tag.go`, `parser/tag_test.go`, `parser/mention.go`
- `extensions/tag.go`, `extensions/mention.go`
- `ast/tag.go`, `ast/mention.go`

---

## 5. Memo Visibility Enforcement

**Visibility type** (`/bench/repo/store/memo.go`, lines 12-22):
- `type Visibility string` with constants `Public ("PUBLIC")`, `Protected ("PROTECTED")`, `Private ("PRIVATE")`.

**Proto enum** (`/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/memo_service.pb.go`, lines 28-38):
- `VISIBILITY_UNSPECIFIED = 0`, `PRIVATE = 1`, `PROTECTED = 2`, `PUBLIC = 3`

**Read access check** (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 39-68):
- `checkMemoReadAccess()`: Archived memos are only visible to creator. Non-public memos require authentication. Private memos require `memo.CreatorID == user.ID`.

**List filtering** (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 218-227):
- Anonymous users: only `PUBLIC` memos returned (`memoFind.VisibilityList = []store.Visibility{store.Public}`)
- Authenticated users viewing all: filter appended as `creator_id == <userID> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`
- Authenticated users viewing another user's memos: `VisibilityList = [Public, Protected]`

**Visibility conversion** (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, lines 350-372):
- `convertVisibilityFromStore()` and `convertVisibilityToStore()` handle bidirectional mapping. Default on creation maps to `Private`.

**Comment visibility** (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 452-464):

**Property extraction via AST walk** (`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, lines 192-241):
